evidence: Source implementation only. No compilation, syntax/import checks, verification, tests, lint, diff checks, timing, benchmarking, queue launch or quality measurement performed.
future_qualification: Not authorized in this session. Map all reachable estimator/representation paths to retained full datasets, versions/hashes, actual dimensions/settings and timed boundaries. Full fit/preparation/synchronization/consumed-output A/B plus neighboring shapes/non-board data and applicable quality gates remain pending.
interactions: N01 through N06 per non-symmetric grow policy
N07 plus N08 for implicit-group and explicit-pair representations separately
N09 plus N10 on the default block32k Yeti route
N11 plus N12 and relevant tree-growth candidates

cards.title: Exact Lossguide speculative batch width 256
affected_estimators: Lossguide categorical, multiclass and ranking callers
cards.mechanism: Select LG_EXACT_BATCH_WIDTH=256 instead of the Apple FAST default128. Existing exact speculative scoring, strict winner order, rollback/replay and final leaf budget remain in control; extra slots trade scratch footprint for fewer batch rounds.
prerequisites: LG_EXACT_BATCH active; legacy approximate batch switch must remain off in both arms
limitations: More candidate scratch may regress memory pressure
Only workloads that use the additional speculative width can change work scheduling
No compile, quality or timing evidence

cards.title: Halve occupancy-derived non-symmetric histogram replicas
affected_estimators: categorical/multiclass/ranking callers reaching the shared non-symmetric driver
cards.mechanism: The non-symmetric driver passes nonsymmetric_work to the standard histogram launcher. With N02, halve the existing hardware/group/leaf-derived replica count, rounding upward to at least one; each replica retains the exhaustive strided row traversal. Explicit replicas_override retains precedence.
prerequisites: No explicit replicas_override for the measured arm
limitations: Already-one-replica work is unchanged
Reduced parallelism may lose on sparse active-leaf sets
Floating accumulation order can change
Alternative quantized-histogram route is outside this candidate

cards.title: Eight-simdgroup vector partition blocks
affected_estimators: GBDT Depthwise and exact-Lossguide callers reaching the DW2 fused row-index partition chain
cards.mechanism: Use DW2_PART_BLOCK=256 instead of512 with four contiguous rows per lane. DW2_PART_CHUNK, chunk-table sizing, flag counts, prefix scans and stable scatters derive from the same constant. All rows and both children remain present.
prerequisites: Existing row-index-only routing must select this path
limitations: More chunk records/scan work may offset occupancy gains
Legacy scalar/stat-moving partition is unchanged
No partition-order or quality evidence has been collected

cards.title: Eight-feature non-symmetric histogram prefix tiles
affected_estimators: categorical/multiclass/ranking callers reaching the shared non-symmetric driver
cards.mechanism: DW2_SCAN_FT changes16 to8 and its shared slab changes4096+8 to2048+8 floats. Each feature still folds every bin in its original order; more independent leaf/stat/feature tiles trade launch count against shared memory residency.
limitations: This is prefix-scan work decomposition, not a replacement for partition-statistics reduction
Noncontiguous or oversized spans retain the existing fallback
Small feature sets can receive no parallelism benefit
cards.idea_revision: N04 is narrowed to the non-symmetric shared histogram prefix scan; shared partition-statistics ownership stays in lane G.

cards.title: Four-simdgroup leaf split descriptor selection blocks
affected_estimators: GBDT Depthwise callers using the device winner-selection/no-level-sync route
cards.mechanism: DW_SELECT_BLOCK changes64 to128. Each worker performs the existing strict-gain leaf selection and ordered prefix rank, then packs its split descriptor. The complete multi-leaf list and creation-order tie semantics stay intact.
limitations: This changes descriptor selection/packing geometry; it does not fuse partition or alter which leaves split
Little benefit expected when very few leaves need descriptors
Larger blocks may lose occupancy
cards.idea_revision: The final N05 experiment targets the multi-leaf split descriptor stage rather than adding another already-fused row application kernel.

cards.title: Two vector groups per row-index cursor copy iteration
cards.mechanism: dw2_copy_back_kernel unrolls two existing strided four-row vector groups per worker iteration under N06. The leaf descriptor and stride are reused, and each group retains its exact boundary guards and copy destination.
limitations: This copies the searcher row-index cursor, not numerical prediction values
Each copy keeps four-wide alignment and scalar boundary stores
Register/code size may outweigh reduced loop control
cards.idea_revision: N06 revised with root approval to searcher row-index cursor copy tiling; numerical leaf prediction application is owned by lane G/root.

cards.title: PairLogit smaller pair/query worker tiles
affected_estimators: GBDT PairLogit ranker; all grow policies reaching PairwiseTargetBuffers
cards.mechanism: The default implicit-group path selects64 physical threads rather than128 per complete-query block. Explicit-pair buffers select128 threads rather than256 for pair derivatives and function-value partials; pair_blocks and the pair reduction/launch widths use the same constant. Every pair, weight and query is retained.
prerequisites: Implicit-group or explicit-pair path selected by the existing public target setup
limitations: The two representations are separate affected workloads; both need later full-recipe coverage
Function-value partial layout changes for explicit pairs; consumers use pair_blocks/q.blocks
Group function-value/magnitude reduction order may change
The64-lane group arm differs from the historical256-versus128 experiment

cards.title: PairLogit ordered endpoint pair unrolling
affected_estimators: GBDT PairLogit ranker; all grow policies reaching PairwiseTargetBuffers
cards.mechanism: Group kernels unroll two ascending shared-memory opponent visits per loop; explicit row accumulation unrolls two ascending endpoint records. Each add, pair multiplicity, endpoint sign and tail visit remains in the original order. This is not the historical rejected each-pair-once algorithm.
prerequisites: For implicit groups keep PL_PAIRS_ONCE disabled equally in A and B
limitations: Compiler may already perform similar unrolling
Repeated document endpoints and extreme margins need later quality coverage
Legacy pairs-once group arm bypasses the modified inner loop for fitting groups

cards.title: Two complete Yeti tasks per scheduled threadgroup
affected_estimators: GBDT YetiRank ranker; all grow policies reaching launch_yeti_rank_with
cards.mechanism: Nonfused32KiB and16KiB block kernels compile-unroll two whole tasks per block with a grid of ceil(task_count/2). Shared allocation is reused with a barrier between tasks. Task IDs, task-derived seeds, four-lane ownership, number of permutations and query boundaries are unchanged; the odd last task is guarded.
prerequisites: YETI_TASK_FUSED disabled equally in both arms (current default)
limitations: Reducing concurrent task blocks may regress short workloads
Sequential fallback and legacy task-fused kernel are unchanged
Legacy direct kernel callers omitting n_tasks_in retain one task per block
No RNG or identity validation performed

cards.title: Eight-output exact Yeti merge tiles
affected_estimators: GBDT YetiRank ranker; all grow policies reaching launch_yeti_rank_with
cards.mechanism: After the existing128-key register sort, each active worker emits eight merged composite keys instead of four. Half of the workers perform co-rank searches; all workers still participate in every inter-pass barrier. The256-worker RNG and pair ownership is unchanged. Implemented in the32KiB block and task-fused kernels.
prerequisites: 32KiB block kernel or existing task-fused route
limitations: The16KiB rank-merge and sequential fallbacks are unchanged
More serial merge outputs per worker can lose throughput
Unique composite keys retain the original tie definition, but that argument is unverified

cards.title: Two-row ranking estimation/search scatter tile
affected_estimators: GBDT YetiRank ranker; all grow policies reaching launch_yeti_rank_with
cards.mechanism: yeti_rank_row_kernel uses128 physical workers for each original256-row logical partial tile, with two row stores per worker. Estimation/search plane layouts and function-value partial count are unchanged. The two-row magnitude sums feed a128-worker reduction, so their FAST fold order can change.
prerequisites: Row-scatter path used by nonfused target evaluation or YETI_EST_REUSE_SEARCH estimation
limitations: Task-fused target evaluation bypasses this row scatter
No estimation iteration, backtracking evaluation or pair sample is skipped
Magnitude fold changes need end-to-end quality qualification

cards.title: Four-simdgroup complete-query mean reductions
affected_estimators: GBDT YetiRank ranker, nonfused query centering
cards.mechanism: A local launch_aft_group_means wrapper selects one128-thread block per complete query. Lanes retain all weighted target terms with strided FMA, then reduce target and weight sums and preserve zero-total-weight behavior. QueryRMSE evaluation and nonfused Yeti centering call the wrapper; the baseline delegates to the original query helper.
prerequisites: Nonfused query mean computation; task-fused Yeti mean computation is unchanged
limitations: A query remains whole regardless of length; no query-size cap or routing threshold
More blocks and idle workers can regress singleton/short queries
Weighted mean reduction order changes, including Yeti centering and downstream sort keys
All full-query quality coverage remains pending
